newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 24.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Columbia/HCA and Tenet face a sticking point in their talks over a possible combination of the health care firms.
* Boeing won tentative approval for its combination with McDonnell Douglas after making a number of concessions.
* Federal Reserve officials spoke to Congress again and did nothing to alter the expectation that the central bank will hold interest rates steady for a while.
* Mallinckrodt agreed to pay $1.9 billion for Nellcor Puritan Bennett.
* General Motors has been forced to close a car assembly conplex because of a transmission plant strike.
* Stock prics moved higher with the Dow climbing to a record 8088.36.
* Cigarette makers are facing fresh pressure after an appeals court cleared the way for the release
* The "yield burning" probe by the IRS has been broadened, in a move by the agency to recover millions of dollars from dozens of municipalities.
* Microsoft plans to significantly increase its spending on sales and marketing and other operations in this fiscal year.
* Several big energy firms parlayed strong refining and marketing results into better-than-expected quarterly profits.
* America Online will provide members phone numbers to telemarketers.
* US Airways Group posted record results.
* Time Warner and News Corp settled their legal battle.
* Digital Equipment fired back with antitrust charges against Intel.
* Northeast Utilities trustees and officers agreed to pay $25 million to settle holders claims that they failed to supervise the firm's troubled nuclear power program.
* Eli Lilly reported stringer-than-expected second quarter sales.
* DuPont posted a 14 percent jump on quarterly net.
* The second quarter net reported by USX jumped 39 percent.
* Minnesota Mining reported lower-than-expected second quarter earnings.
* United Technologies and AlliedSignal posted double digit gains in second quarter net.
* Sweden's Volvo acquired General Motors' remaining 13 percent common stock interest in the two companies' North American heavy trusk venture.
* Bond prices slipped following the strong rally Tuesday.
* Some short sellers are bowing to the stength of the market and quitting the business. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
